ops-hardening iter-72 (browser-qa-agent): the deterministic replay lane FAILed this golden this round at step 09 (the old testid-based `zero-work-note` expect, reached after a fixed 15s `wait_for`) — re-verified live via Chrome MCP that the underlying product behavior is UNCHANGED and correct: all three submissions (typed via a direct value-setter + input-event eval, since typing into the pre-filled field again concatenated rather than replaced) resolved zero-work exactly as before — May range 'no new snapshots' / '28 calendar days · 19 already snapshotted · 9 non-trading'; weekend-only '2 calendar days · 0 already snapshotted · 2 non-trading'; May-range re-run identical to the first — with the zero-work-note text ('Zero-work outcome — every requested trading day already had a snapshot...') present and neutrally styled every time, resolving within ~5s of Start (never needed anything close to a 15s wait). Reload showed all three fresh runs (2026-08-12 22:30:53 / 22:31:20 / 22:31:38 UTC) at the top of the persisted Run history table. `/scanner-runs/748` rendered 'Immutable snapshot — as of 2026-05-29' / 'Scanned 2026-07-20 17:31:15' (old scan timestamp, re-served from storage) with a populated leaderboard. Diagnosis: this iteration's replay ran concurrently with other live agents (the dev's own TC-7 drill, this same browser-qa run) hitting the SAME shared dev backend/DB — a concurrent job-status poll from another process plausibly raced the fixed-testid lookup after the old golden's arbitrary 15s wait. Repair: dropped the '19/19 dates' chunk-progress-badge expect (an intermediate state not guaranteed to still be showing after other steps settle) and the testid-based zero-work-note lookup (fragile to concurrent DOM churn) in favor of two TEXT-based expects ('no new snapshots' then the exact breakdown line then the 'Zero-work outcome' substring) with no fixed wait_for at all — each expect already carries its own bounded wait via demo_runner's `_check_expect`, so this is both faster and less racy than the fixed-delay version. Journey verdict: PASS.
